title: Which file goes in which loader and folder
hook: Checkpoint, diffusion model, text encoder, VAE: what each one holds, which folder feeds which menu, and how to tell them apart when the file name tells you nothing.

verified.claim: Each folder name maps to its model folders: diffusion_models to unet and diffusion_models, text_encoders to text_encoders and clip, controlnet to controlnet and t2i_adapter.
Menus list known extensions only, include subfolders in the name, and the first folder wins for a duplicate. .gguf and .txt were left out.
verified.ref: folder_paths.get_filename_list and get_full_path on a throw-away tree

verified.claim: A file name not in the menu gives value_not_in_list.
verified.ref: execution.validate_prompt with a made-up checkpoint name

verified.claim: A checkpoint loader given a denoiser-only file warns and returns a model with no CLIP, and a VAE object that raises when used.
UNETLoader accepts a whole checkpoint and takes the denoiser out: the comment reads 'Allow loading unets from checkpoint files'.
The key names in the play and the lab are ones ComfyUI's detection and loading code reads.
Each menu's folder is the one named in that node's INPUT_TYPES.
The docs say to put files in the type's subfolder, press r to refresh, and that GGUF needs community custom nodes.

unchecked: We did not press r in a browser. The server side checks the folder's modified time on each call, and the editor's refresh is taken from the docs.
The lab's kind test is ours, a teaching simplification. ComfyUI's real detection is far longer.
We did not load real files for the combinations in the last table: they come from reading comfy/sd.py.
